senses.gloss:
विमद

VIMADA . A truthful King. Once a princess named Kamadyū accepted vimada as her husband at her svayaṁvara marriage. The Kings and princes who were present became jealous of vimada and prepared for war. The helpless vimada praised the aśvinīdevas. The gods defeated the enemies and gave the bride to vimada. (ṛgveda, Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 17, Sūkta 117).

विमल १

VIMALA I . A King. vimala who was the King of South india was the son of sudyumna. (bhāgavata, skandha 9).

विमल २

VIMALA II . A King of the city of Ratnātaṭa. At the time of the horse-sacrifice of śrī rāma, this King rendered a good deal of help to śatrughna. (padma purāṇa, pātāla Khaṇḍa, Chapter 17).

विमला

VIMALĀ . A female calf born from rohiṇī, the daughter of surabhi. rohiṇī had two daughters called vimalā and analā. (M.B. Ādi Parva, Chapter 66, Stanza 67).

विमलपिण्डक

VIMALAPIṆḌAKA . A nāga (serpent) born to prajāpati kaśyapa by his wife kadrū. (M.B. Ādi Parva, Chapter 35, Stanza 8).

विमलाशोकतीर्थ

VIMALĀŚOKATĪRTHA . A holy place. It is stated in mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Chapter 14, Stanza 69, that he who spends a night in this holy place, observing celibacy, would attain heaven.

विमलतीर्थ

VIMALATĪRTHA . A holy place. In the lakes of this place, fishes having the colour of gold and of silver play. Mention is made in mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Chapter 82, Stanza 87, that those who bathe in this holy bath would get remission of all their sins and would get to the world of indra.

विमलोदका

VIMALODAKĀ . Once brahmā performed a sacrifice on the Himālayas. sarasvatī attended this sacrifice, on which occasion she adopted the name vimalodakā. (M.B. śalya Parva, Chapter 88, Stanza 29).

विमोचन

VIMOCANA . A holy place on the boundary of kurukṣetra. By taking bath in this tīrtha and leading a life without anger, the sins incurred by receiving bribes would be remitted. (M.B. Vana Parva, Chapter 83, Stanza 161).

विमुच

VIMUCA . A South Indian hermit. (mahābhārata, śānti Parva, Chapter 208, Stanza 28).

विमुख

VIMUKHA . A hermit of ancient india. This hermit is member of the assembly of indra. (M.B. Sabhā Parva, Chapter 7).
